# Nitrogen and its Compounds

## Core ideas and reasoning

Nitrogen gas is relatively unreactive at room temperature because its triple bond is strong. In the Haber process nitrogen and hydrogen react reversibly to form ammonia: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. The forward reaction is exothermic and reduces gas moles, so high pressure favours yield while lower temperature favours equilibrium yield but slows reaction. Industrial operation uses a compromise temperature, pressure and iron catalyst, followed by cooling to separate ammonia and recycling unused gases. Ammonia is very soluble in water and produces an alkaline solution. It turns damp red litmus blue and forms white ammonium chloride fumes with hydrogen chloride. Ammonium salts release ammonia when warmed with a strong alkali. Nitric acid is an oxidising acid and its metal reactions differ from simple dilute-acid hydrogen production. Nitrogen compounds are important in fertilisers, but runoff can promote eutrophication; link the nutrient increase to algal growth and oxygen depletion during decomposition.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Write the balanced Haber process equation.

N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). It is reversible and exothermic in the forward direction.

### Example 2

State a test for ammonia gas.

It turns damp red litmus paper blue. It also forms white fumes of ammonium chloride with hydrogen chloride gas.

### Example 3

Write the ionic equation for ammonia released when an ammonium salt is warmed with alkali.

NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → NH₃(g) + H₂O(l). Warm gently in supervised conditions; do not smell directly.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
